title: Symmetry and Monotonicity of y = -4*sqrt(x)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graph of y = -4*sqrt(x), determine whether it has any symmetry, and specify the intervals where the function is increasing or decreasing.

steps.title: Identify the Domain and Lack of Symmetry
steps.explanation: The square root requires x >= 0. Because the domain [0, inf) contains no negative inputs and its outputs are all <= 0, the graph lies entirely in Quadrant IV (plus the origin) and has no symmetry.
steps.why: A graph confined to a single quadrant cannot be symmetric about either axis or the origin.

steps.title: Compare Function Values on [0, inf)
steps.explanation: Because sqrt(x) is strictly increasing on [0, inf), multiplying by the negative constant -4 reverses the inequality, making -4*sqrt(x) strictly decreasing on [0, inf).
steps.why: Multiplying a strictly increasing function by a negative scalar yields a strictly decreasing function.

steps.title: Summarize Graph and Intervals
steps.explanation: The graph starts at (0, 0) and falls through (1, -4) and (4, -8) in the fourth quadrant, decreasing on [0, inf).
steps.why: Every increase in x >= 0 produces a larger positive value of sqrt(x) and hence a more negative value of -4*sqrt(x).
